title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent→configuration pipeline: an artifact-grounded paired evaluation and lessons from a ceiling effect
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) to test whether integrating an automated network verifier (and automated rollback) into an LLM intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments. Using gpt-5-mini under a shared-initial-candidate policy across 150 paired intents (300 episodes), we ran two pipelines per task: LLM-only (baseline) and LLM+verifier-block (guarded). All 150 generated candidates were accepted by the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) in both pipelines (150/150 valid per pipeline), producing a degenerate paired contingency (n11=150, n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered McNemar test is therefore uninformative (p=1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0,0.0]). We report complete, artifact-backed execution and scoring traces (selected file hashes are cited inline), diagnose why a ceiling effect occurred (100% identical shared-initial outputs and validator acceptance predicates as archived), and give concrete, artifact-grounded recommendations (adversarial/stateful task banks; multi-verifier/multi-model comparisons) to reveal verifier-sensitive failure modes. All raw transcripts, validator traces, scoring JSONs, analysis scripts, and SHA256 hashes are archived and referenced.

sections.introduction: Motivation. Mapping natural-language operator intent into low-level device configuration via LLMs is a promising NetOps automation path, but erroneous enactments can cause outages or security exposures. Community proposals therefore advocate verifier-and-rollback machinery around LLMs to bound risk. Research question. CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 asked: Does integrating an automated network verifier (block-on-violation) into an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline reduce per-task unsafe enactment rates relative to LLM-only in a paired emulated NetOps benchmark? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, deterministic paired experiment with an archived artifact bundle (preregistration SHA-256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04). (2) A concise, evidence-linked report of execution, scoring, and validator acceptance predicates used in the run (representative scoring JSON: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json, sha256=974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14). (3) An artifact-grounded diagnosis of a ceiling effect and prescriptive, reproducible next-step designs to stress verifier-sensitive failure modes.
sections.related_work: We situate this study among (i) LLM-based intent translation and intent-driven configuration for NetOps (e.g., Nguyen et al., 2024; related OpenAlex records W7114889968, W7155247165, W7161354925), (ii) generate–validate–repair paradigms and test-in-the-loop repair in code and configuration synthesis, and (iii) network-change verification/digital-twin approaches (Batfish/NetKAT/HS families). Our contribution is empirical and reproducibility-focused: we supply a fully archived, preregistered paired run and analyze why a verifier effect was not observable under the selected benchmark and validator.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. We preregistered CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 (see preregistration SHA-256 above). Design: paired confirmatory experiment, 150 confirmatory tasks stratified by intent ambiguity (benign / ambiguous / partially-specified). Execution harness and artifacts. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model recorded as gpt-5-mini (execution manifest). Generation policy: shared_initial_candidate — one initial generation call per task, at most one repair call per task (frozen). Model calls used: 150 (one per task; execution manifest reports model_calls_used=150). Validator and scoring. Executed verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id field present in scoring JSONs). The validator exposes and records the following acceptance fields per episode: required_command_count, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, violation_codes, and valid==true/false (see representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256=974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14). Primary estimand and analysis. Primary estimand: per-task unsafe-enactment rate difference (baseline minus guarded). Analysis: paired exact McNemar two-sided test with Bonferroni adjustment as preregistered; complementary paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Contamination and exclusions. Auto-exclude rules and contamination detectors were enforced (analysis/contamination_summary.csv sha256=389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). All deterministic retry, exclusion, and stopping rules from the preregistration were followed.
sections.results: Execution and scoring summary (artifact-backed). Episodes executed: 300 (150 paired tasks); completed successfully with zero failed episodes (execution_manifest). Model calls used: 150. Scoring outcomes: baseline valid-configurations = 150/150 (100.0%); guarded valid-configurations = 150/150 (100.0%). Paired contingency: n11=150, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256=c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e). Statistical result. The preregistered McNemar test is degenerate given zero discordant pairs; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0 and the paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Key deterministic observations (artifact-linked): (A) Shared-initial identical outputs across conditions: per the execution manifest and response-file hashes, the baseline and guarded responses were identical for all 150 tasks (100% identical per-task response hashes; representative identical-hash pair: execution/responses/task-000001-baseline.txt and execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt share SHA256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080). (B) Validator acceptance predicates and fields are encoded in each scoring JSON and show violation_count==0 and valid==true for every confirmatory episode (representative scoring JSON: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256=974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe6...). Contamination detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks (analysis/contamination_summary.csv sha256=389227f0...).
sections.discussion: Why the ceiling effect occurred (artifact-grounded diagnosis). Two joint, artifact-backed causes explain the observed ceiling: (1) Generator determinism under the frozen prompt/policy: the shared_initial_candidate policy produced the same generated candidate for both pipelines on every task (100% identical per-condition response hashes); consequently the guarded pipeline had no variant candidate to block. (2) Validator acceptance predicates, as implemented in deterministic_netops_validator_v5, were satisfied by every generated candidate: scoring JSONs show required_command_count satisfied and violation_count==0 in all confirmatory episodes (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256=974cab2a...). These facts are preserved in the execution bundle and deterministically reconcile (see analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Inferential consequence. Because n10=n01=0, the preregistered inferential test is uninformative: we cannot conclude the verifier would reduce unsafe enactments in a regime that produces discordant outputs. This is an evidence-backed null observation about this execution regime, not a general claim about verifier utility. Practical lessons and reproducible recommendations (artifact-grounded): (i) joint benchmark+validator design: create adversarial/stateful task banks that target dependency and temporal invariants recorded in the validator traces (difficulty patterns such as make_before_break_uplink_switchover and paired_link_atomic_mtu_change appear as 'pattern' entries in scoring JSON difficulty fields and should be used to craft stress cases); (ii) multi-verifier and multi-model matrix: compare different verifier families (Batfish-style, header-space/SMT tools, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5) across multiple LLMs to surface verifier-sensitive failure modes; (iii) introduce live-state, timing, or transient invariants rather than purely syntactic acceptance predicates; (iv) retain the preregistered paired design, contamination detectors, and reproducibility logging, while intentionally injecting verifier-challenging examples. Reproducibility pointers (selected artifacts and hashes): preregistration JSON SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04; model_configuration.json sha256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa; representative scoring JSONs: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256=974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json sha256=9ae4c9db62d09a44b547cc57e191582c1e303ab95a91fe5c44085fa5cdbd0701. The full execution manifest and the analysis artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv sha256=c2ba9cdb..., contamination_summary.csv sha256=389227f0...) are archived and referenced in the bundle.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and ran a deterministic paired study to test whether adding a verifier and automated rollback reduces unsafe LLM-generated NetOps enactments. In the executed regime (gpt-5-mini, shared_initial generation, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, 150 confirmatory pairs), every generated candidate satisfied the validator and both pipelines produced 150/150 valid configurations; the preregistered inferential comparison is therefore untestable in this run (paired difference = 0.0 pp; exact McNemar p = 1.0). The scientific value is the artifact-rich lesson: (i) benchmarks and validators must be co-designed to expose verifier-conditional failure modes, (ii) single-model, single-validator, synthetic-task regimes can produce ceiling effects that prevent meaningful confirmatory inference, and (iii) we release the full artifact bundle so others can run adversarial/stateful follow-ups. We provide concrete, reproducible next-step designs likely to reveal verifier value (adversarial/stateful tasks; multi-model and multi-verifier matrices). Selected artifact pointers and SHA256 hashes are provided inline to enable immediate verification of every principal claim.

disclosure_statement: Human and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family and supplied the initial master prompt and autonomy constraints before the autonomy lock. Pre-lock: collaborative development produced reusable harness components and rehearsal scripts; pre-lock experimental results were not used as confirmatory evidence. Post-lock autonomy: after the lock the AI autonomously performed literature review, research-question selection, machine-readable preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001, preregistration SHA-256=66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04), deterministic experiment implementation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, automated peer-review checks, and finalization. Models and orchestration: experiments used a single hosted model recorded as gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses in the execution manifest). Adapter/orchestration family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Prompts and generation semantics: the run used a shared_initial_candidate policy (one initial generation call per task; at most one repair call per task) as frozen in the preregistration; exact frozen prompt text and adapter instructions are archived in the execution bundle (see execution/model_configuration.json sha256=1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Verifier and validator: the executed validator is recorded as deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and its per-episode traces and acceptance outputs are archived in execution/scoring/*.json (representative file execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256=974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14). The preregistration discussed Batfish-style open-source verifiers as conceptual references; the actual run used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (artifact-backed). Preregistered procedures: sampling plan (150 confirmatory tasks), exclusion and contamination detectors (auto-exclude non-RFC1918 public IPs; exact-match fingerprinting), retry policy, stopping rules (>2% contamination abort), and statistical analysis (paired McNemar with Bonferroni adjustment) were all recorded and enforced. Execution artifacts and reproducibility: the run produced 300 episodes (150 paired tasks), used 150 model calls, and completed with no failed episodes. All raw outputs, model-call traces, scoring JSONs, validator traces, analysis scripts, and sha256 hashes are archived and referenced in execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis artifacts (e.g., analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256=c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e). Human editing: no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock; all manuscript revisions requested by reviewers were implemented autonomously using the archived artifacts. Deviations and restarts: none beyond automated retries described in the preregistration. Limitations: the study used synthetic, emulated tasks and a single model and validator; archived contamination detectors are heuristic and cannot guarantee absence of subtle training-data leakage.
limitations: Ceiling effect in confirmatory run: both pipelines produced validator-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, making the preregistered primary and secondary inferential comparisons untestable in this regime.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic and may not exercise live-state, timing, or adversarial invariants present in production NetOps.

Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM families or verifier implementations (e.g., Batfish-style tools).

Validator specificity and acceptance predicates: the validator used here enforces the acceptance predicates visible in the archived validator traces (e.g., required_command_count, parsed_command_count, violation_count==0). Those predicates differ across verifier families and likely influenced the ceiling effect; full validator configuration is archived (execution/model_configuration.json sha256=1acce925...).

Construct validity: the chosen validator-detected 'unsafe enactment' metric is an imperfect proxy for operational harms such as transient reachability loss, timing-dependent outages, or side effects not encoded in the validator rules.
Contamination detection limits: deterministic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate the possibility of subtle training-data leakage.
